title: Tensor evaluation and flat sections at a partition object
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with pullbacks, a strict initial object $\varnothing$, and disjoint finite coproducts stable under pullback. Assume the component inclusions of every finite coproduct are a covering, including the empty covering of $\varnothing$. Fix an object $W$ such that every covering of $W$ refines a finite coproduct decomposition of $W$. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, $A=\mathcal O(W)$, and $E(M)=M(W)$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume also that $W$ is terminal in $\mathcal C$ and $E$ is exact. For arbitrary module sheaves $M,N$ the section tensor pairing
$$M(W)\otimes_A N(W)\longrightarrow (M\otimes_{\mathcal O}N)(W)$$
is an isomorphism, where the sheaf tensor is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Its presheaf takes $\varnothing$ to zero and finite coproducts to products, under the canonical component identification
$$(\prod_a M_a)\otimes_{\prod_a R_a}(\prod_a N_a)\cong\prod_a(M_a\otimes_{R_a}N_a).$$
The pairing is natural and compatible with ordinary associativity, symmetry and the unit $A=\mathcal O(W)$, using the same pure-tensor and scalar formulas on both paths. If $F$ is a flat module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $F(W)$ is a flat $A$-module. More precisely, for every finite relation $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i=0$ in $F(W)$, including $n=0$, there exist $m\ge0$, $y_j\in F(W)$ and $b_{ij}\in A$ with $x_i=\sum_jb_{ij}y_j$ and $\sum_i a_i b_{ij}=0$. For the kernel sheaf $H=\ker(\mathcal O^n\xrightarrow{(a_i)}\mathcal O)$, such data can be obtained from a finite tensor sum $\sum_j h_j\otimes y_j\in H(W)\otimes_A F(W)$ mapping to $(x_i)$, with $h_j=(b_{ij})$. No flatness of $F(U)$ at other objects is assumed.

proof.text: For any module sheaf $L$, the sheaf axiom on the empty cover gives $L(\varnothing)=0$; for the ring sheaf it gives the zero ring. For $U=\coprod_aU_a$, any family of sections on the components is matching: distinct-component pullbacks are $\varnothing$, while each same-component pullback is $U_a$. Unique gluing on the component cover gives $L(U)\cong\prod_aL(U_a)$ and $\mathcal O(U)\cong\prod_a\mathcal O(U_a)$. The identifications respect addition and scalar multiplication because restriction does. These assertions include the empty coproduct.

proof.text: Here is the required component tensor calculation, directly from balancing. For a finite family put $R=\prod_aR_a$, $M=\prod_aM_a$, $N=\prod_aN_a$. The canonical map $\Phi$ sends $m\otimes n$ to $(m_a\otimes n_a)_a$. Let $\iota_a$ extend a component vector by zero and let $e_a\in R$ be its component idempotent. The rule $u\otimes_{R_a}v\mapsto\iota_a(u)\otimes_R\iota_a(v)$ is $R_a$-balanced: extend a scalar by zero in $R$ and apply the $R$-balancing relation. Adding these maps gives $\Psi:\prod_a(M_a\otimes_{R_a}N_a)\to M\otimes_RN$. Then $\Phi\Psi=1$ on each component, and $\Psi\Phi(m\otimes n)=\sum_a e_am\otimes e_an=\sum_a m\otimes e_an=m\otimes n$, since $e_a^2=e_a$ and $\sum_ae_a=1$. Thus $\Phi$ is an isomorphism. For an empty family both sides are zero. Apply this calculation to step 1: the presheaf $P(U)=M(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}N(U)$ sends finite coproducts to products and $\varnothing$ to zero.

proof.text: By the module-sheafification statement, $P^\#$ is the abelian-group sheafification with its extended $\mathcal O$-action and a linear unit. By the underlying-sets sheafification statement for abelian groups, its underlying set sheaf is the set sheafification of $|P|$. Step 2 verifies the initial-value and finite-product hypotheses of the partition-refinement lemma. Apply that lemma at $W$ to obtain a bijection $P(W)\to P^\#(W)$. It is $A$-linear, hence an $A$-module isomorphism. The definition of the sheaf tensor identifies this unit map with the pairing in the item. In Lean, the public partition-refinement theorem fixes the value universe to max u v w. For the independent coefficient universe here, apply the same local-injectivity and local-surjectivity argument directly: use its covering_refinement helper to obtain a precoverage covering, refine that covering by a finite partition, and use the tensor presheaf product bijection and sheaf separatedness. The module sheafification unit is locally bijective after forgetting to sets. Compose its bijection with the inverse of tensorObjIsoSheafification.

proof.text: Write $\theta_{M,N}$ for the pairing just proved invertible. For module maps $f,g$, both naturality paths send $m\otimes n$ to the section represented by $f(m)\otimes g(n)$; hence they agree by additivity. The associativity diagram sends $(m\otimes n)\otimes p$ on each path to the section represented by $m\otimes(n\otimes p)$, the symmetry diagram sends $m\otimes n$ to $n\otimes m$, and the left and right unit diagrams send $a\otimes m$ and $m\otimes a$ to $am$. These are the ordinary tensor associator, braiding and unitors: locally their maps are exactly these formulas, which respect the balancing relations and therefore sheafify by the universal property. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, and each $\theta$ is surjective, so these checks prove all diagrams, including diagrams involving an iterated sheaf tensor. The unit is $\mathcal O(W)=A$. Concretely, the forgetful functor has the lax monoidal structure right-adjoint to module sheafification. Its tensorator is the stated pairing, and its unit map is the identity by the adjunction triangle. Lax monoidal naturality, associativity, unitality and the braided-adjunction identity give the four formulas.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03ER (definition-flat); finite-partition specialization of Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Lemma 4.1(1)

proof.text: Let $\sum_i a_ix_i=0$ be a finite relation in $F(W)$. Define $q:\mathcal O^n\to\mathcal O$ by $q_U((c_i))=\sum_i(a_i|_U)c_i$, using the unique $U\to W$ (here terminality of $W$ is used). Put $H=\ker q$. The sectionwise-kernel statement gives $H(W)=\ker(A^n\to A)$, and $H\to\mathcal O^n\to\mathcal O$ is exact. Flatness of $F$ means precisely that $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}F$ is exact; apply this exact functor and then the assumed exact functor $E$. Step 3 and its naturality identify the result with the exact sequence $H(W)\otimes_AF(W)\to A^n\otimes_AF(W)\to A\otimes_AF(W)$. The finite-free identification sends $e_i\otimes y$ to the vector with $y$ in position $i$, with inverse $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes x_i$; the unit identification sends $a\otimes y$ to $ay$. Consequently the last arrow is $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_ix_i$. Exactness therefore supplies a preimage $t\in H(W)\otimes_AF(W)$ of $(x_i)$. Use the proved comparison siteSheafTensorRightIso [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] to transfer flatness from the explicit site tensor to the monoidal tensorRight functor. In fact evaluation preserving kernels suffices: tensor the kernel sequence by the exact tensor functor, then apply the kernel-preserving evaluation functor. The first map is still monic, so Mathlib's map_of_mono_of_preservesKernel gives exactness at the middle. Thus the assumed full exactness of evaluation is not needed in this proof, and its hypothesis is preserved.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03ER (definition-flat); finite-partition specialization of Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Lemma 4.1(1)

proof.text: Write $t=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j\otimes y_j$, possible by the algebraic tensor-product construction, and write $h_j=(b_{ij})\in H(W)\subseteq A^n$. Its image is $(\sum_jb_{ij}y_j)_i=(x_i)_i$, while membership in the kernel says $\sum_i a_ib_{ij}=0$ for each $j$. This is exactly the required trivialization, with the specified tensor preimage. The equational criterion now implies that $F(W)$ is flat over $A$. If $n=0$, choose $m=0$ and $t=0$; zero coefficients cause no change to the argument. If $W=\varnothing$ or $A$ is the zero ring then all section modules concerned are zero, and the same formulas apply. No assertion about flatness of $F(U)$ was used.
